headline: Nothing big today, don't bother chasing the Riemann proof
summary: No new tools made the cut today. The local model Inkling 2 Mini keeps getting more buzz, but I've already recommended it.

items.title: Garry Tan's software factory experience
items.signals: Garry Tan tweet, 724 likes · no link in the source, so info is limited
items.what: Garry Tan runs Y Combinator, the well-known startup accelerator. He retweeted a post from @capydotai about Capy's iOS version, which is looking for testers on TestFlight (Apple's app beta testing platform). He said he does about half of his work with "this" tool, together with his "software factory" (his own workflow for using AI to churn out software in bulk). He didn't say much about what the tool can actually do.
items.meaning: Right now it's just one famous person saying nice things, plus a mobile beta. I couldn't find an official write-up for Capy, so it doesn't really affect you.
actions: If you want to try it, find the "Capy for iOS" tweet from @capydotai on X and reply in the comments to ask for a TestFlight spot, like they ask.
deep_dive: His exact words: out of the desktop, phone and cloud ways of using it, this is the one that feels best to him "right now". That's just his personal opinion, with no comparison data.
I couldn't find Capy's official features, pricing or supported regions, so I can't compare it to Claude Code or codex, which you already use.
